subject: Civil Engineering
title: Pounding Between Buildings
description: A 60-second lesson on Pounding Between Buildings.

hook.text: Two buildings stand inches apart. In an earthquake, they sway at different rates and collide.

buildup.text: Each building has its own natural period. Shorter ones sway fast, tall ones sway slow.

discovery.text: When they hit, columns at the contact point take enormous impact — causing local collapse.

twist.text: Floor slabs of adjacent buildings rarely align — a floor hits the other building's column.

climax.text: Seismic gaps — separation joints — keep buildings apart during maximum expected shaking.

punchline.text: Buildings need personal space. In earthquakes, neighbors too close become enemies.

quiz.question: Why is floor misalignment dangerous during building pounding?
options: It causes the floors to collapse on top of each other
One building's floor slab strikes the other's column, causing concentrated damage
The gap between floors lets earthquake waves enter the interior
